title: Personal LLM inference mini-tracker (Riley) Feb 2026
content:
Quick personal mini-sheet to track short LLM inference perf experiments.
Purpose: capture quick runs, baseline numbers, and next steps so I don't lose context while iterating on batching/quant profiles.
Notes: numbers are noisy — use as directional. focus on median p50 latency for interactive SLOs and throughput for batch workloads.

Table (CSV-style):
experiment_id,date,model,variant,quantization,batch_size,seq_len,avg_latency_ms,throughput_tps,tokens_per_sec,mem_gpu_gb,notes,status
exp-2026-02a,2026-02-12,redwood-7b,base,fp16,1,256,42,24,1536,12.3,baseline single-stream,complete
exp-2026-02b,2026-02-13,redwood-7b,base,4-bit,1,256,48,26,1660,9.6,quantized 4-bit,more variance than fp16,draft
exp-2026-02c,2026-02-14,redwood-7b,sharded,4-bit,4,256,85,85,5400,12.0,continuous batching helps throughput,draft
exp-2026-02d,2026-02-15,vicuna-13b,base,int8,1,512,130,9,4608,22.5,latency high on 13b,baseline for larger model,complete
exp-2026-02e,2026-02-16,redwood-3b,base,fp16,8,128,18,120,15360,6.1,cheap low-latency option,complete
exp-2026-02f,2026-02-18,redwood-7b,cache-enabled,4-bit,1,512,55,22,11264,9.8,prefix cache reduced repeated compute,in_review

Quick interpretation:
- 4-bit quant gives cost savings (lower GPU mem) but increases p50 latency ~10-20% on short sequences; variance higher on small batch sizes.
- Batching (batch_size >=4) improves throughput linearly up to GPU saturation but increases tail latency — need to test p95 for interactive flows.
- For seq_len 512, models with KV cache + prefix cache show better tokens/sec for repeated contexts.

TODO / next runs:
- Run p95/p99 for exp-2026-02b and exp-2026-02f (especially 4-bit runs) across 1000 requests.
- Try q4_0 vs q4_1 quant variants (if runtime supports) and record mem/latency tradeoffs.
- Test autoscale and burst behavior for redwood-7b sharded setup: create load pattern 200rps for 2m.
- Add cost estimate column (tokens/sec * price_per_token) for clearer economics.

Scratch notes:
- Link to infra PR with batching changes: github:redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321 (see bench script in /bench/scripts/run_multi.sh)
- Jira INF-1234 covers quantization rollout plan — schedule canary after perf gating.

Notes to self: keep experiments small, stash full-run logs in /tmp/llm-bench-YYYYMMDD-<id>.tar.gz and reference path in final report. If numbers look promising, propose test matrix for Redwood Optimize to recommend quant profiles per workload.

End of mini-tracker (lightweight, iterate fast).
